items.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: You know I didn’t see that whole documentary. I saw some of the early ones and enjoyed learning so much about Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: I love the Duke’s music. When I grew up though in terms of emotionally I was more drawn to Count Basie’s band. And there was something about the rhythmic unison feeling of that band, it was like one pulsing organism, that emotionally got to me even more than Duke’s band and Duke’s writing, although unquestionably he’s one of the towering geniuses of the music, clearly.

You know I didn’t see that whole documentary. I saw some of the early ones and enjoyed learning so much about Louis Armstrong. A lot of stuff I didn’t really know. So I was really pleased and I saw that as a big plus. From talking to my musical colleagues that apparently he left the last 50 years of music history for an hour and a half segment, I didn’t even end up finishing it so I can’t comment on the sweep of the whole work. I guess in his defense he never pretended that this was supposed to be a definitive…
